description: This course covers foundational and advanced topics in Natural Language Processing including tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and sentiment analysis using libraries like NLTK, spaCy, and Hugging Face Transformers. Students will study statistical and deep learning models such as Hidden Markov Models, Conditional Random Fields, and BERT for tasks like machine translation and text generation. The course also explores language models, dialogue systems, and information retrieval using standards like Unicode and XML. Topics include word embeddings, sequence-to-sequence models, and transformer-based architectures. Students will implement and evaluate NLP systems using Python and frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow.

clos.text: Define tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, and stopword removal techniques for preprocessing text data.
Describe the architecture and training process of recurrent neural networks and transformer models for sequence modeling.
Explain the principles of part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, and dependency parsing using probabilistic models and rule-based systems.
Apply sentiment analysis and text classification algorithms using pre-trained models like BERT and RoBERTa for real-world datasets.
Design and implement a chatbot or dialogue system using NLP techniques and evaluate its performance using metrics like BLEU and ROUGE.

topics: Introduction to NLP and its applications
Text preprocessing techniques: tokenization, stemming, and lemmatization
Introduction to statistical NLP models: HMM and CRF
Part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition
Introduction to transformer architectures and BERT models
Deep learning for text classification and sentiment analysis
Information retrieval and query processing techniques
Dialogue systems and chatbot design principles
Machine translation and neural machine translation models
Text generation and sequence modeling techniques
Ethical considerations in NLP and bias mitigation strategies
Evaluation metrics and performance analysis for NLP systems
Final project presentation and course review
